title: Zero to Unbeatable
tagline: Three things people call AI on one board: hand-written rules, real learning, and where both run out
card_blurb: Three opponents on one tic-tac-toe board. First, eight if/else rules a person wrote out — it has played zero games, it tells you which rule it just used, and you cannot beat it. Then a learner that starts from nothing and reaches the same unbeatable play after ~20,000 games. Then nine boards at once, where neither approach scales. Same exhaustive search proves both of the first two.
description: **Zero to Unbeatable** — a single-file, phone-first demo of the three different things people call AI, on one tic-tac-toe board. **Step 1** is a hand-written if/else ladder of eight rules (win, block, fork, block the fork, centre, opposite corner, empty corner, empty side): it has played zero games, it names the rule behind every move and the squares that triggered it, and a depth dial switches rules off so a room can beat the two-rule version and watch the app draw the exact game it loses. **Step 2** is tabular reinforcement learning from zero knowledge, trained in visible 5,000-game bursts between which the student plays it; frozen eras with per-era scoreboards, a brain inspector overlaying the learned value of every square, and a "what it learned" card with before/after heatmaps. Both steps end up provably unbeatable and the app proves both with the same exhaustive search over every reachable game line — 1,384 lines against the rules, about 15,000 against the learner — which is the whole point: identical play, opposite origins. The page says plainly that for a board this small the hand-written rules are the better engineering, and that learning earns its keep only where the rules cannot be written. **Step 3** trains the learner on nine boards at once — a mark per turn on any unfinished board, first to five boards — to show what breaks when the world gets bigger: on one board a position recurs 10x per training burst, on nine it recurs 1.06x, so no table could ever learn it, and there is no proof on offer. No network, no AI service, nothing baked into the learner. Includes a printable demo guide.
